hints.content: The opposite angles in ANY inscribed quadrilateral are supplementary.  [[☃ explanation 1]]

options.explanation:
The measure of an inscribed angle is $\frac{1}{2}$ of the measure of the arc that it intercepts.

$\pink{\text{m}\angle R} = \frac{1}{2}(\text{m} \stackrel{\LARGE{\frown}}{BEA})$  
$\blue{\text{m}\angle E} = \frac{1}{2}(\text{m} \stackrel{\LARGE{\frown}}{ARB})$

When we add the measures of the two angles together, something interesting happens:

$\pink{\text{m}\angle R}+ \blue{\text{m}\angle E} = \frac{1}{2}(\text{m} \stackrel{\LARGE{\frown}}{BEA}) + \frac{1}{2}(\text{m} \stackrel{\LARGE{\frown}}{ARB})$

$\pink{\text{m}\angle R} + \blue{\text{m}\angle E} = \frac{1}{2}(\text{m} \stackrel{\LARGE{\frown}}{BEA} + \text{m}\stackrel{\LARGE{\frown}}{ARB})$

The sum of those $2$ arcs makes up the entire circle, which is $360^\circ$.

$\pink{\text{m}\angle R} + \blue{\text{m}\angle E} = \frac{1}{2}(360) = 180$
